chunks: And everything in this book that is narrated from Abu Habib Najiyah, I have transmitted it from my father - may Allah be pleased with him - from Sa'd ibn Abdullah, from Mu'awiyah ibn Hakim, from Abdullah ibn Al-Mughira, from Mathna Al-Hannat, from Abu Habib Najiyah.

key_terms.أَبِي حَبِيبٍ نَاجِيَةً: Abu Habib Najiyah, a specific narrator
key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: May Allah be pleased with him, a honorific for the father
key_terms.سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Sa'd ibn Abdullah, a key narrator in the chain
key_terms.مُثَنَّى الْحَنَّاطِ: Mathna Al-Hannat, a narrator in the chain

ai.seo_question: What is the transmission chain for narrations from Abu Habib Najiyah in this hadith collection?
ai.summary: This passage functions as a crucial methodological preface in *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih*, where Shaykh al-Saduq explicitly defines the specific *isnad* (chain of transmission) he relies upon for all narrations attributed to Abu Habib Najiyah, thereby ensuring textual consistency and authenticity. By tracing the lineage through notable figures like Saad ibn Abdullah and Mu'awiya ibn Hakim, al-Saduq underscores the reliability of the Kufan scholarly tradition and provides readers with a clear framework for evaluating the veracity of these reports within Shia jurisprudence.
